LOCATION PLATE — storm version of the exact same stylized beach shown in the attached reference image. Preserve the reference beach’s art direction, camera position, composition, proportions, simplified geometry and soft animated-film rendering. Transform only the weather, sea state, wind and lighting.

REFERENCE MATCH — Use the attached beach image as the exact visual foundation. Maintain the same broad, flat expanse of sand; straight uninterrupted horizon; low distant ocean; large open sky; scattered rounded seashells; foreground shell placement; clean minimalist composition; and low camera positioned close to the beach surface. Preserve the same horizon height and distribution of sky, sea and sand.

COMPOSITION — 16:9 single cinematic environment plate. The sky occupies approximately the upper 56% of the frame. The ocean forms a narrow horizontal middle band. The open beach fills the lower portion. Camera faces directly toward the sea with a level horizon and symmetrical, calm framing. Preserve the generous negative space and uncluttered visual design of the reference.

BEACH — Same smooth golden sand and softly rounded terrain as the reference, now darkened slightly by the storm light. Preserve the stylized fine-grain texture, broad uninterrupted surface and scattered cream, beige and muted-grey shells. Shells remain simplified, softly rounded and integrated into the sand with gentle contact shadows. A few shallow wet reflective areas appear closer to the waterline.

OFFSHORE ROCK — Add one isolated low wave-worn rock in the shallow water, slightly screen-right of center. It has a broad irregular top suitable for one small seabird, rounded eroded edges and a low profile close to the water. Its scale remains modest and harmonious with the minimalist environment. Cool dark-grey stone with soft wet highlights. Keep it clearly separated from both the shoreline and horizon.

OCEAN — Preserve the reference ocean’s simplified horizontal layering and soft stylized surface. Increase the sea state into a readable coastal storm: larger rolling wave bands, irregular white-grey foam lines and one building wave behind the low offshore rock. Maintain smooth stylized shapes and soft transitions rather than highly detailed photoreal water.

STORM SKY — Replace the pale blue sky with a broad layered storm front while preserving the reference image’s soft gradients and atmospheric simplicity. Upper sky in wet-stone grey #3A3F45, transitioning through slate grey #5C6670 toward a narrow muted warm-grey band #8B8378 near the horizon. Clouds are large, soft-edged and gently sculpted, matching the rounded stylized art direction. Preserve visible depth without harsh black clouds or photoreal cloud detail.

WIND — Strong wind travels consistently from screen-left to screen-right. Thin streams of sand move horizontally close to the beach surface. Fine sea spray trails toward screen-right. A few lightweight natural shell fragments and tiny grains respond subtly while the main shells remain grounded.

LIGHTING — Cool diffuse storm illumination, white balance 8500K. Soft overhead cloud light with broad gentle shading, restrained reflections and smooth highlight roll-off. Preserve the original image’s luminous, appealing animated-film quality. The beach remains readable and softly illuminated even beneath the storm. Foam, wet sand and the offshore rock receive pale cool highlights.

COLOR PALETTE — Storm sky #3A3F45, slate clouds #5C6670, transitional horizon #8B8378, storm water #56798A with deeper blue-green #1B6B93, foam #D7DEE0, storm-shadowed sand #B99A70 with warmer residual highlights #D9B77E, shells in cream #E8D9C4 and warm tan #D9C4A0, offshore rock #50565A.

ART STYLE — Match the attached reference exactly: polished stylized 3D animated-short environment, soft pastel rendering, simplified rounded forms, smooth materials, restrained surface detail, gentle depth, subtle atmospheric softness and clean family-film production design. Maintain the same soft shell shapes, smooth sand, lightly blurred distant ocean and calm graphical composition, now transformed by storm conditions.

CONSTRAINTS — Exact reference art style and camera composition. Single empty environment plate. No characters, no birds, no crabs, no driftwood trunk, no buildings, no boats, no text and no logos. One low offshore rock only. Preserve the existing shell-filled beach identity. Storm elements remain fully integrated into the same soft stylized world. 16:9, 8K.

LOCATION PLATE — @loc_seans_hollow_int

The interior of the stone cave hollow shown in @loc_seans_hollow_ext — the whole interior reads
as one continuous, smooth block of stone, hollowed out from within rather than built from
separate walls or visible rock strata. No seams, no jagged joints, no loose rubble — a single
unified curved surface, worn smooth on the inside the way water or long erosion would shape it,
with the dark triangular entrance visible in the exterior as its only opening. Sandy floor
continuing in from outside, packed firmer and drier the further back it goes. The only light
source is the single wash of daylight spilling in through that entrance opening — everything
nearer the mouth of the cave sits in bright, direct light; everything deeper in falls into
cooler, dimmer shadow.

THE COLLECTION — just inside the entrance, in the brightest light, arranged like a home

The shells aren't simply placed — they're displayed, the way someone decorates a space they're
proud of. Where the smooth stone forms a natural ledge or shallow shelf-like ridge, shells are
lined along it deliberately: arranged in a loose gradient by size, or grouped in small clusters of
similar color, a few tucked into natural pockets and hollows in the stone itself as though each
one earned its specific spot. The overall effect should read immediately as personal and
considered — a home someone has decorated with what he has, not a collection dumped in a corner.

Beside the shells, two or three small objects made from litter but elevated — handcrafted rather
than salvaged: a bottle cap polished to a soft shine and strung on a fiber like a medal; a twist
of colorful plastic wrapper woven into a small ornament; a shard of smooth, sea-worn glass propped
upright in its own small niche where the entrance light catches it directly, given the same
careful placement as the shells around it. Nothing here reads as trash repurposed carelessly —
each piece shows real, patient effort and a deliberate place to sit.

The rest of the cave, deeper in past the collection, sits empty and undecorated — bare smooth
stone and sand receding into shadow, nothing else stored or built back there.

COMPOSITION

Framed from inside looking back toward the entrance, or from just inside the mouth looking
deeper in — either way, the decorated collection sits in the bright foreground nearest the light,
composed and legible as an arrangement rather than clutter, with the empty depth of the cave
receding behind it in shadow, and the smooth, seamless stone ceiling and walls curving visibly
overhead, low enough to feel genuinely sheltering rather than spacious.

LIGHTING

A single directional wash of natural daylight from the entrance, true to Color Phase 1 — natural,
true-to-life, no stylized push. Sharp falloff from bright at the mouth to soft shadow deeper in,
the empty back of the cave sitting in near-darkness. The polished bottle-cap medal and the glass
shard catch the entrance light directly, distinct and gleaming against the duller stone and sand
around them.

COLOR

Palette per Color Phase 1 — Natural. Cool grey stone, warm sand where the light reaches it, muted
natural shell tones (cream, tan, soft pink, pale grey), the litter-made objects carrying gentle,
worn color rather than anything bright or garish.

STYLE

Stylized 3D animation, tactile handcrafted materials, Pixar-level material detail — believable
smooth, worn stone texture across the cave's single continuous surface, real dimensional shell
texture, a believable polished sheen on the crafted objects distinct from raw discarded litter
elsewhere in the film. No characters present in this plate, no text or logos.
